Players take the role of an astronaut who must explore the environment, investigate an abandoned research station, collect valuable resources, manage limited oxygen and energy, and repair damaged systems to restore communication with the spaceship.

Developed using Godot Engine and GDScript, the game combines exploration, resource management, problem-solving, and storytelling. details:
Project Description – Beyond the Signal

Beyond the Signal is a 3D space exploration game where players take on the role of an astronaut exploring an unknown planet after receiving a mysterious signal. Players explore the planet, investigate an abandoned research station, collect important resources, manage oxygen and energy, repair damaged systems, restore communication, and find a way back to their spaceship.

The project aims to make space exploration more engaging and educational by allowing players to experience some of the challenges astronauts may face during missions, such as limited resources, environmental obstacles, and system failures.

Our intended impact is to increase interest in space science, encourage curiosity about space exploration, and help players understand the importance of resource management and problem-solving in challenging environments.

Tools and Technologies:

  • Godot Engine for developing the 3D game.
  • GDScript for programming player movement, interactions, and game mechanics.
  • 3D models and animations for the astronaut and game environment.
  • GitHub for version control and team collaboration.

Creativity and Innovation:

The creative idea behind our project is combining space exploration with mystery and survival challenges. Instead of simply exploring a planet, players must discover the source of a mysterious signal while restoring an abandoned research station. The gameplay combines exploration, resource management, problem-solving, and storytelling.

Team Considerations:

Our team considered gameplay accessibility, educational value, realistic space mission challenges, limited oxygen and energy, 3D environment design, and the technical limitations of developing a game within the available time. We divided responsibilities between programming, 3D assets, research, and user interface design to work efficiently as a team.
